# Interest calculations

Interest is money earned on a saved principal. In these examples there are no fees, deposits, or withdrawals.

## Example A

The rate is 5%.

Principal: 1,000. After one year: 1,000 × 1.05 = 1,050.

## Example B

The rate is 5%.

Principal: 500. After one year: 500 × 1.05 = 525.

## My learner note

Do not change my shortcut: convert the percentage to a decimal first.

## Practice

Try calculating one year of interest on a principal of 200 at 4%.

markdown:
# HTTP caching ## Introduction Caching is the operational retention of previously retrieved representations governed by freshness and validation semantics. A user agent may reuse stored response entities subject to cache directive constraints and conditional revalidation. ## Request lifecycle 1. A browser asks for a resource at a URL. 2. The server responds with a body and headers. 3. The browser may store the response. 4. On a later visit, freshness rules determine whether it can reuse that response immediately. 5. A stale response may be validated with the origin before reuse. A fresh cached response can avoid a network request entirely. A validated response can avoid transferring the resource body while still requiring a network round trip. ## Reference - A cache key distinguishes stored responses. - Vary tells a cache which request headers influence the response selection. - no-store prevents storing the response. - no-cache permits storage but requires validation before reuse. - private permits storage by a private cache but excludes shared caches. - A 304 response has no replacement representation body. ## Interactive visualization ```learnfold-visualization
1 download
``` ## My learner note My production stylesheet is app.a91f.css. Keep this filename in my notes; do not replace it with an example filename. ## Practice Explain the difference between avoiding a request and avoiding a response body.
